source: EU Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition (ECGT) Directive (EU) 2024/825, amending the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive 2005/29/EC

rules.regulation: Directive 2005/29/EC Annex I point 4a (inserted by Directive (EU) 2024/825; applies from 27 September 2026): generic environmental claims are banned unless the trader can demonstrate recognised excellent environmental performance
rules.explanation: A generic environmental claim (such as 'eco-friendly', 'green' or 'sustainable') is prohibited in the EU unless the trader can demonstrate recognised excellent environmental performance relevant to the claim, for example an EU Ecolabel. Otherwise say exactly what is environmentally better, in the same sentence. Note: 'green' also matches the colour, so check the sentence.

rules.regulation: Directive 2005/29/EC Annex I point 4c (inserted by Directive (EU) 2024/825; applies from 27 September 2026): claims that a product has a neutral, reduced or positive greenhouse gas impact based on offsetting are banned
rules.explanation: In the EU you may not claim that a product is climate or carbon neutral, or has a reduced or positive climate impact, on the basis of offsetting emissions. Describe only actual reductions in the product's own emissions, with the figures and how they were measured.

rules.regulation: Directive 2005/29/EC Annex I point 2a (inserted by Directive (EU) 2024/825; applies from 27 September 2026): a sustainability label must be based on a certification scheme or established by a public authority
rules.explanation: A brand's own sustainability label, badge or collection name is banned unless it is based on a third-party certification scheme or set up by a public authority. Remove the label, or replace it with the specific certified fact.

rules.regulation: Directive 2005/29/EC Annex I point 4b (inserted by Directive (EU) 2024/825; applies from 27 September 2026): a claim about the whole product or business when it concerns only one aspect
rules.explanation: Claiming that an entire product, range or business has an environmental quality when it is true only of one aspect (one material, one process) is banned. Name the one aspect the claim is true for.

rules.regulation: Directive 2005/29/EC Article 6(2)(d) (as amended by Directive (EU) 2024/825; applies from 27 September 2026): future environmental performance claims need a detailed, realistic implementation plan verified by an independent expert
rules.explanation: A claim about future environmental performance is misleading unless it is backed by clear, objective, publicly available and verifiable commitments in a detailed implementation plan that an independent third-party expert monitors. Keep the claim only if you can evidence that plan.

rules.regulation: Directive 2005/29/EC Annex I point 10a (inserted by Directive (EU) 2024/825; applies from 27 September 2026): presenting requirements imposed by law as a distinctive feature of the offer
rules.explanation: Presenting something every competitor must do by law as if it were a special feature of your product is banned. Remove it, or state something that goes beyond the legal minimum.
